text:
Alex C (Product): quick sync — Acme just pushed: they need P99 < 200ms for chat completions and want a committed plan. asking the group: which perf work do we prioritize next sprint? latency hotpath vs throughput batching vs cost (quant+cache). thoughts?

Maria G (Eng): can we get rough RICE inputs? impact looks high for Acme but effort/risks vary per workstream.

Cheng L (ML): short take: quantization (int8/4-bit) -> best cost per token but risk of subtle quality regressions. needs 1-2 weeks of evals + rollout flags.

Sam R (SRE): latency-focused changes (kv cache, prefix cache warm pools, kernel selection) reduce tail but need warm capacity. may increase infra spend if we keep warm GPUs.

Evan T (Product): also consider sequencing: shipping latency wins first helps PLG signals and onboarding. cost wins can be behind a toggle.

Lara P (Solutions): Acme cares about predictable latency more than raw cost. they told Solutions they're willing to sign Dedicated if we can provide SLA and fallbacks.

Alex C (Product): propose a quick RICE sheet in thread. everyone drop numbers 1-10 for Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort (low=10 high), I'll compute.

Maria G (Eng): adding numbers for latency-hotpath: Reach=7, Impact=9, Confidence=6, Effort=4

Cheng L (ML): quant+pack: Reach=6, Impact=7, Confidence=5, Effort=3

Sam R (SRE): batching/throughput work: Reach=8, Impact=6, Confidence=6, Effort=5

Evan T (Product): my numbers (business lens): latency-hotpath R=8 I=9 C=7 E=4; cost (quant) R=5 I=7 C=5 E=3

prio-bot: RICE calc (Alex): latency-hotpath score = (Reach*Impact*Confidence)/Effort -> (8*9*7)/4 = 126

Alex C (Product): rough math says latency-hotpath wins. but notes: RICE hides operational cost (warm pools). need explicit SLA-cost tradeoff doc.

Maria G (Eng): suggestion: split latency work into two slices: A) kernel + routing improvements (low-risk, quick wins), B) warm-pool SLA (higher cost, longer). prioritize A in next sprint, start spike for B.

Cheng L (ML): agree. also run small evals for int8 on canary models concurrently (2 eng days) so we don't block.

Sam R (SRE): operational ask: if we commit to P99 < 200ms for Dedicated, we should propose an auto-fallback policy to lower-tier model when overloaded. keeps user-facing latency stable.

Lara P (Solutions): note for Acme: fallback to a smaller model is acceptable if we maintain response semantics. they prefer graceful degradation over errors.

Evan T (Product): action items: Alex to write SLA-cost briefing for execs + runbook. Maria + Cheng: scope kernel/routing slice A for next sprint. Sam: spike warm-pool sizing and fallback policy. Lara: prep Acme-facing note.

Alex C (Product): added to roadmap doc: <https://redwood.app/drive/roadmaps/inference-prio> — please add estimates by EOD.

Cheng L (ML): small note: put quant eval testset under /evals/latency-cost to track regressions.

Maria G (Eng): can someone tag the required perf tests? p95/p99 synthetic + real-prod sampling.

Sam R (SRE): I'll add perf tests to CI and create a daily perf-run. will need a staging pool.

Evan T (Product): consensus: prioritize latency hotpath (slice A) next sprint, start parallel spikes for warm pool sizing and quant evals. we can revisit cost optimizations in 2 sprints.

Alex C (Product): cool — if nobody objects, I'm locking this as the decision. will send follow-up with acceptance criteria:
- kernel/routing slice A: measurable P95 down by 30% on chat flows vs baseline
- warm-pool spike: sizing estimate + cost delta for 99.9/99.95 targets
- quant eval: quality delta < 1% on key metrics or gated

Lara P (Solutions): noted. i'll sync with Acme and feed constraints back.

Maria G (Eng): quick FYI: blocking risk — third-party kernel patch might take legal/ops time. will surface if it becomes an issue.

Alex C (Product): thanks all. follow-up doc + tickets from me shortly. :white_check_mark:
note: This thread captures a short product prioritization debate using RICE and sequencing considerations for inference performance.
